title: En lugar de + infinitivo: un modelo económico distinto

sections.content: En lugar de + infinitive (instead of doing X) is the natural structure for describing a deliberate policy switch -- exactly what import substitution industrialization was: a choice to stop doing one thing and start doing another. It's used only when the subject of both actions is the same. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: ¿Por qué seguir dependiendo de importar manufacturas en lugar de producirlas dentro del propio país?
items.english: Why keep depending on importing manufactured goods instead of producing them within the country itself?

items.spanish: En lugar de exportar materias primas baratas para importar después productos caros, los países debían fabricar ellos mismos buena parte de lo que compraban.
items.english: Instead of exporting cheap raw materials to later import expensive products, countries had to manufacture much of what they bought themselves.

items.spanish: En lugar de simplemente esperar a que la demanda internacional se recuperara, países como Brasil, México y Argentina comenzaron a levantar barreras arancelarias.
items.english: Instead of simply waiting for international demand to recover, countries like Brazil, Mexico and Argentina began raising tariff barriers.

items.spanish: En lugar de limitarse a recaudar impuestos y mantener el orden, muchos gobiernos comenzaron a invertir directamente en industrias estratégicas.
items.english: Instead of limiting themselves to collecting taxes and keeping order, many governments began investing directly in strategic industries.

sections.content: En lugar de que + subjunctive exists for cases with two different subjects, but it's rare -- in practice, en lugar de + infinitive (same subject throughout) is what you'll meet by far the most often, as every example above shows.
